messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected for hosted inference (p99 > 6s over 10m). Symptoms: streaming stalls, tail token delays, elevated paging backlog, and prefix cache hit-rate collapse. Paging queue growth observed in us-west-2. Incident ID INC-1965. Pinged oncall.

sara (oncall): taking this. first pass: p50 looks ok, p95 up modestly but p99 spike to ~6-8s. streaming requests show stalls at token boundaries (client sees long pauses mid-stream). notifying eng-sre + runtime. assigning triage. @mike can you pull cache and paging metrics?

mike (eng-sre): pulling metrics now. short snippets: 
```
prefix_cache_hit_rate 0.11  # 10m ago ~0.78 earlier today
prefix_cache_miss_rate 0.89
active_paging_backlog 420 shards
streaming_tail_ms_p99 6120
streaming_tail_ms_p95 980
kv_retries/sec +120%
```
Ran: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api?series=prefix_cache.*&range=15m" | jq .
Looks like hit rate collapsed after a deployment ~3h ago. paging workers are saturated trying to fill misses.

jia (eng-ml): that matches a change earlier today — we rolled prefixtap-v2 (hash salt + shard rebalancing) at 2026-03-15T10:12Z. The intention was to reduce hot-shard skew but we didn't update the warmup/warm-cache job to the new key derivation. New keys have effectively cold caches.

sam (runtime): proposed mitigations (ordered by safety/speed):
1) enable fallback routing for streaming to routed-model-medium to avoid stalls while we recover caches. Command: `redwood routes set --policy fallback routed-model-medium`
2) flip feature flag to restore old prefix hashing: `ffctl set prefixtap_v2.enabled false` (safe toggle; rollback path validated)
3) temporarily raise prefix cache TTL to 15m to keep existing entries longer: `cfgctl put /cache/prefix/ttl 900`
4) run synthetic warmup to repopulate top prefixes: `scripts/warmer --source recent_high_qps --rate 300/s --concurrency 50`
5) if needed, throttle canary traffic or pause further prefixtap rollouts.

elaine (support): customer impact — atm three enterprise customers (acme-inc, medlytics, educloud) are reporting degraded interactive experiences and increased timeouts (acme ~12% requests > 5s, medlytics ~8%, educloud ~5%). CS alerted; we prepared mitigation notes for support.

omar (cs): acme is on a high-visibility contract; they're already seeing user escalation. recommend we prioritize fallback routing + flag flip first.

sara (oncall): executing mitigations in that order. toggling fallback routing now.

sam (runtime): ok on routing toggle. doing the flag flip next — note: the flag is global but guarded by canary gates. will set globally but watch for KV churn.

sara (oncall): `ffctl set prefixtap_v2.enabled false` -> done (1965000065).

mike (eng-sre): seeing immediate effect on cache keys — cache hit-rate climbing from 0.11 -> 0.32 within 3m after warmup started. paging backlog stabilizing. snippet: 
```
1965000120 prefix_cache_hit_rate 0.32
1965000180 prefix_cache_hit_rate 0.45
1965000240 active_paging_backlog 180
1965000300 streaming_tail_ms_p99 1180
```
Looks like warmup + rollback helped. p99 dropped from ~6s to ~1.2s.

jia (eng-ml): confirming that the old hash path is serving again. we should add an automated warmup step to the prefixtap rollouts; the new rollout missed the warmup binding.

mike (eng-sre): also observed error logs on the KV layer during peak: 
```
KVERR: prefix-shard-mismatch key=0xab12 shard=22 expected=17
KVWARN: eviction-surge threshold exceeded
```
Those align with cold keys landing on unexpected shards (because clients started using new derivation before caches warmed).

sara (oncall): customer mitigation status: acme - reduced timeout rate to ~2.5% after routing/flag flip; medlytics ~1.7%; educloud ~1.2%. Support notified.

elaine (support): sending templated communication to impacted customers summarizing mitigation actions and ETA for postmortem.

sam (runtime): follow-up actions I'm creating:
- add warmup job to prefixtap rollout pipeline (must run for X minutes + verify hit-rate > 0.6)
- extend canary criteria to include prefix_cache_hit_rate & paging_backlog thresholds
- add circuit-breaker to fallback routing for tail latency spikes

mike (eng-sre): ops follow-ups:
- add alert for sudden prefix_cache_hit_rate delta > 0.25 in <30m
- add metric to deployment dashboard showing warmup status per shard
- document runbook: if hit-rate drops and paging backlog > 200, enable routing fallback and assess flag rollback.

jia (eng-ml): will open PR for rollout changes today. also adding a verification test to the rollout job that runs the warmer against the new key derivation.

sara (oncall): handing active monitoring to mike for the 2hr stabilization window. I'm logging this in incident tracker INC-1965 with short notes.

mike (eng-sre): taking over monitoring. will keep slack updates every 15m until stable.

sara (oncall): handoff -> mike (eng-sre). thanks everyone. final note before handoff: resolved enough for now but keep paging/streaming SLOs under watch. please add postmortem with timeline + remediation owners. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: RESOLVED? status still open (monitoring). auto-reminders scheduled for 1h and 24h.

mike (eng-sre): marking incident as "mitigated" in tracker (1965000345). will follow up with full postmortem and action items.

sara (oncall): leaving notes for next rotation: check `prefix_cache_hit_rate`, `active_paging_backlog`, and `streaming_tail_ms_p99` in first 30m of shift. prefixtap flags are currently rolled back.

elia (support): (later) draft of customer-facing summary saved at https://confluence.internal/incidents/INC-1965-draft

mike (eng-sre): closing updates for now — monitoring looks green, will open postmortem and owners assigned.
